samples.text:
The map shows the town of Leenford and two places, A and B, where a new supermarket could be built. Overall, site A is near to the town and the houses, but site B is far away in the south-east corner.

The town centre is in the middle of the map and Queen's Road goes through it from north to south. Most of the houses is in the north-west and the north. In the south there is a river and a railway, which both go from west to east, and there is an industrial estate near the railway. A motorway goes from north to south in the east of the town.

Site A is in the north-east. It is next to the housing in the north and near to the end of Station Road. Site B is on the east of motorway, in the south-east. It is to the south of the railway and the river and it is near a industrial estate and farmland. So site B is more far from the houses than site A.
samples.why: Overview present · both sites described with relevant location detail · mechanical linking (Also, So) · adequate but repetitive vocabulary · several errors in prepositions, comparatives, articles and agreement.

samples.text:
The map illustrates two proposed locations, labelled A and B, for a new supermarket in Leenford. Overall, site A lies close to the town's residential areas and centre, whereas site B is situated on the south-eastern outskirts, beyond the motorway and the railway.

The town centre occupies the middle of the map, with Queen's Road passing through it from north to south and the station on its eastern side. Housing is concentrated in the north-west and the north, while a park lies to the west of the centre. The River Leen and the railway line both run across the southern part of the town, and a motorway runs from north to south in the east.

Site A is located in the north-east, directly east of the northern housing area and just west of the motorway. It lies slightly to the north of the end of Station Road, which leads westwards across the town, north of the centre.

By contrast, site B is in the far south-east corner, on the eastern side of the motorway. It lies south of both the river and the railway, and its nearest neighbours is the farmland to the north and the industrial estate to the west.
samples.why: Clear overview comparing the two sites · each site located accurately relative to key features · good referencing and contrast language · some less common vocabulary · mostly accurate with an agreement slip.

samples.text:
The map presents two possible sites, A and B, for a new supermarket in the town of Leenford. The key difference is that site A would be located within the built-up area, close to housing and the town centre, whereas site B lies on the periphery, separated from the town by the motorway, the river and the railway.

The town is centred on a commercial area crossed by Queen's Road, with the station immediately to the east and a park to the west. Residential areas occupy the north-west and north, and Station Road runs eastwards from the western edge, north of the centre, as far as the motorway, which bisects the eastern part of the map from north to south. The River Leen and the railway both cross the southern half of the town.

Site A sits in the north-east, adjoining the northern housing area and bordered by the motorway to the east. It lies just north of the eastern end of Station Road, the main route leading westwards across the town.

Site B, in contrast, occupies the far south-eastern corner, on the eastern side of the motorway and south of both the river and the railway. Its only neighbours are farmland to the north and, across the motorway, an industrial estate.
samples.why: Incisive overview of the core contrast · precise location of both sites relative to roads, housing and barriers · sophisticated cohesion · accurate, varied vocabulary (periphery, bisects, adjoining) · complex structures handled without error.
